title: Copy, override three projects, re-optimize, diff

blocks.text: Riverbend Water (invented for this practice) answers its engineers' what-if questions the way this module does: never by editing the plan under review. `whatif.py` already has the model: `solve(plan, projects)` picks at most one start year per water main within each year's budget, maximizing value, and applies the plan's overrides as bounds (`("start_in", y)` fixes the year, `("out", None)` keeps the main out).
Write the two missing functions; `what_if` uses them.

items: `copy_with_overrides(base, plan_id, overrides)`: a new `Plan` with `base`'s budgets and overrides, the new `overrides` added on top (a new override on a project replaces the old one), and `parent_id` naming `base`. The base must come out of a what-if exactly as it went in.

`diff(a, b)`: from plan `a` to plan `b` (each `{pid: start year}`), the projects `b` selects that `a` does not, the projects `a` funds that `b` defers, and the projects both fund in different years, as `(pid, a's year, b's year)`. Each list sorted by project id.

blocks.text: The main test overrides three mains on a copy, re-optimizes both plans and checks the diff. About eight lines in all.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from whatif import Plan, Project, diff, solve, what_if

pipes = [
    Project("P-1", (200, 100), {2030: 600, 2031: 550}),
    Project("P-2", (150,), {2030: 300, 2031: 280, 2032: 260}),
    Project("P-3", (250,), {2031: 420, 2032: 390}),
    Project("P-4", (100,), {2032: 140}),
]
base = Plan("S-1", {2030: 400, 2031: 400, 2032: 400})

print("base plan:", solve(base, pipes))
trial, changes = what_if(base, "S-2", {"P-1": ("start_in", 2031), "P-4": ("out", None)}, pipes)
print("trial S-2 overrides:", trial.overrides, "parent", trial.parent_id)
print("trial plan:", solve(trial, pipes))
print("diff base to trial:", changes)
print("diff of two small plans:", diff({"P-2": 2030}, {"P-2": 2032, "P-3": 2031}))

cases.says: the copy carries the base's override and the three new ones, and solves to the overridden plan
from the base to the copy, two projects are deferred and one is shifted two years later
the base plan keeps its own overrides after the what-if, and the copy names it as parent
a project funded in both plans in different years is shifted, not deferred and selected
a project only the second plan funds is selected

origin.section: When Overrides Make a Scenario Infeasible, the Trail Finds Which Ones

concepts: a what-if copies the plan, adds overrides as bounds, re-optimizes both and diffs them project by project
